Row.Text: Cassava Pit

Cassava, also known as yuca or tapioca, differs from the other major root crops in that its edible roots are not organs of dormancy and do not appear to have a natural function in the preservation of the plant through the dry season. Thus, the roots are not inherently adapted for survival and once harvested they deteriorate rapidly, developing a vascular discoloration within a few days which renders the roots unpalatable. One means of storing fresh cassava roots which has been used since ancient times by the Amerindians of Amazonia is to bury the harvested roots in pits or trenches, a technique probably derived from the common practice of leaving the cassava unharvested.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Since the advent of the more advanced techniques of cold storage and freezing it has become possible to export cassava. It can be made into a flour that is used in breads, cakes and cookies. In Brazil, farofa, a dry meal made from cooked powdered cassava, is roasted in butter, eaten as a side dish, or sprinkled on other food. In Taiwanese culture, later spread to the United States, cassava "juices" are dried to a fine powder and used to make tapioca, a popular starch used to make bubbles, a chewy topping in bubble tea. Alcoholic beverages made from cassava include cauim (Brazil), kasiri (Venezuela, Guyana, Suriname), parakari or kari (Venezuela, Guyana, Surinam), and nihamanchi (indigenous peoples of South America).
*this is updated in another file*

The Cassava Pit is an early source of additional Food, as well as increasing the value of settling near Plant Bonus Resources that yield it. The Granary's base bonuses are considerably strengthened. One potential use of having much more flat food from your Cassava Pit is in working a Specialist slot that you otherwise would not be able to afford. Whilst the value of this bonus becomes relatively weak as the game goes on, an extra 5% Food Kept retains value, allowing higher population values to be reached. Finally, there is a delayed effect unlocking at the Refrigeration Technology, suggesting a particular research path as you enter the endgame.
Yatiri

Yatiri are medical practitioners and community healers among the Aymara of Bolivia, Chile and Peru, who use in their practice both symbols and materials such as coca leaves. There are many factors at play in a person's calling to become a yatiri. The confirmation of this calling, however, is marked by a lightning strike, which typically happens to an unmarried Aymara out herding the flocks in the Mountains.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Christian church has also often ostracised the Yatiri, perceiving their role to be superfluous in modern religious practice, and a form of paganism. This has changed as current government officials openly support Yatiri presence in events that formerly might have had a Catholic chaplain under the terms and practice of the Concordat with the Holy See. Nevertheless, normal practice for most Andean people mixes practices from both traditions, for example in the cha'lla, a blessing bestowed on any form of property, often done with both sacrifices to the Pachamama and Catholic prayers.
*this is updated in another file*

The Yatiri boosts your Faith output, especially when there are nearby Mountains. Perhaps the more significant bonuses though are military: healing Units that are in the City like an early Hospital, and spawning the Coca Luxury Resource, whose Monopoly bonus increases the attack and defense of all Units. The two bonuses can be harnessed together with the Zealotry Belief.
Kgotla

A kgotla is a public meeting, community council, or traditional law court of a Botswana village and in rural Lesotho and South Africa. It is usually headed by the village chief or headman, and community decisions are always arrived at by consensus. Headmen usually work as the advisers to the chief. No one may interrupt while another is having their say. Because of this tradition, Botswana claims to be one of the world's oldest democracies.
*this is updated in another file*

Constabularies are a niche Building often reserved for your largest Cities. The Kgotla deepens and expands that with a notable bonus to certain Specialists and Food from nearby Pastures. The second aspect is however totally different, giving Production to Courthouses everywhere in your Empire. Together with the +1 Happiness bonus, this allows a Bantu player to use the width of their Empire to provide a large boost in all their Annexed Cities, encouraging war.
Ghat

Ghat are series of steps leading down to a body of water or wharf, such as a bathing or cremation place along the banks of a river or pond, the Ghats in Varanasi, Dhobi Ghat or the Aapravasi Ghat. Raj Ghat, in particular, was the cremation site for Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi and numerous political leaders after him. The word is also used in some places outside the Indian subcontinent. For example, in George Town, Penang, Malaysia, the label "Ghaut" is used to identify the extensions of those streets which formerly ended in ghats before the reclamation of the quayside.
*this is updated in another file*

Ghat are an optional or "leaf" Building like the Baths they replace. As a result, Rivers are considerably more valuable to the Bharata Group and there is a strong incentive to settle them. In particular, they can generate hugh amounts of Faith, meaning your Cities should be located on Rivers, even if it comes at a cost.
Teutonic Order

The Teutonic Order is a Catholic religious institution founded as a military society c. 1190 in Acre, Kingdom of Jerusalem. The Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem was formed to aid Christians on their pilgrimages to the Holy Land and to establish hospitals. Its members have commonly been known as the Teutonic Knights, having historically served as a crusading military order for supporting Catholic rule in the Holy Land and the Baltic Crusades during the Middle Ages, as well as supplying military protection for Catholics in Eastern Europe.
*this is updated in another file*

The Teutonic Order should be thought of as a Faith Building. Until the advent of Gun and Armor Units, the bulk of your army belong to the "General Chapter", and earn Faith from XP amongst other bonuses. Further, Buildings that must be Purchased with Faith, such as Belief Buildings, are stronger for you, and you receive Faith from Barracks. Together, military investment can be turned into religious output. If you wish to create a virtuous cycle, you can further consider the Zealotry Belief.
Dwór

Dwór are mansions that were historically owned by the szlachta of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. More modest homes of provincial nobility were called dwórek, or "little manors". The countryside was the preferred location for one's residence, as the nobility, following the sarmatism ideology, felt contempt for the cities. Early renaissance mansions were based on a rectangular design, with corner chambers (alkierze) and a porch. The style evolved over time, and larger palaces boasted many guest rooms, a chapel, and even their own opera house. In the 17th and 18th centuries, a view emerged that identified particular manor architecture with 'Polishness', treating it as native and unique. It gained particular traction in the 19th century during the period of Romanticism.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Lithuania was occupied by Soviets in 1944, the manor houses themselves and their remaining land were nationalized and repurposed, mostly as schools, living quarters or administrative centers of collective farms. In Poland, the ideologically-driven nationalization policies and architectural preservation guidelines enacted during the early years of the communist Polish People's Republic contributed to the destruction of many manor houses. Before World War II, there were tens of thousands of manors. Today, only over 2,000 remain, often in very poor condition.

The Dwor continues the Polish niche of constructing two buildings at once, giving a Free Opera House in the City. If you had already constructed an Opera House, you will instead be refunded the Production as an instant boost. However the major effect is its yields from unlocking Policies, which grant a large local boost to the key yields of Food, Production, and Border Growth Points. When the Polish Unique Ability grants you two additional tenets, this will cause an explosion in growth, so be ready! Whenever your borders expand, you will receive increased yields compared to the standard buildings, a small bonus that over time pays for the maintenance and opportunity cost of building the Dwor.
Djéli
National Exhibit

Classical history serves a source of interest, tourism, and indeed national pride for the successor states of these ancient empires. In this, archaeological and further museal attractions are key. For example the Museo Nazionale Romano is a museum, with several branches in separate buildings throughout the city of Rome, Italy. It shows exhibits from the pre- and early history of Rome, with a focus on archaeological findings from the period of Ancient Rome. The Similarly the Ethnikó Archaiologikó Mouseío in Athens houses some of the most important artifacts from a variety of archaeological locations around Greece from prehistory to late antiquity and contains the richest collection of Greek Antiquity artifacts worldwide.
*this is updated in another file*

The National Exhibit goes beyond the Culture bonuses of the Royal Collection. Moreover the Theming bonus can become much larger. Either all-Art or all-Artifact themings work, with 5 extra yields if consecutive Eras. However the best is half-and-half Art-Artifact, with consecutive Eras topping out at a mighty 25 yields. Indeed, one should strongly consider the Artistry Policy that increases Theming bonuses in light of this Cultural Group component. Finally, all your Galleries and Museums become more lucrative, which means you must not slack on Cultural infrastructure either, another point in favor of Artistry.
Sobor

In Eastern Orthodoxy a sobor is a formal gathering or council of bishops together with other clerical and lay delegates representing the church to deal with matters of faith, morality, rite, and canonical and cultural life. Such ecumenical councils have proved central in determining the theology. For example Eastern Orthodoxy holds that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and rejects the Filioque clause ("and the Son") added to the Nicene Creed by the Latin Church, on the grounds that no council was called for the addition. [NEWLINE][NEWLINE]An Orthodox Divine Service is chanted in its entirety by the clergy, the choir, and the congregation from the start of the service to the end. Byzantine chants are associated with the Eastern Roman Empire's period (AD 330 to 1453) and developed from Jewish and Syrian traditions in the early-Christian Church. Northern Slavs, however, have used simpler tonal systems evolved through the sundry local types of Znamenny chant. Russian liturgical chants (including some Ukrainian and Balkan churches) evolved from the Kievan Rus people in AD 988. In the 14th century, Russian elements began to be used in the church. By the 16th century, Russian chants had many links to the Byzantine style.
*this is updated in another file*

The Sobor has additional bonuses for Musicians and Great Works, and as a Building it supports both of those directly as well. The two Music slots available are some of the earliest for Theming Great Works of Music! If you can manage to produce two in the same Era you will maximize the bonus, but consecutive Eras is only slightly worse. This can be tough early on, so consider the Artistry Free Great Person Policy. There is also a global boost to Border Growth Points based on Faith, which promotes certain Instant Yield strategies such as the Policies of the Authority Policy Branch.
Palm Mill

Almost 90% of the world's palm oil is produced in Indonesia and Malaysia. Along with coconut oil, palm oil is one of the few highly saturated vegetable fats and is semisolid at room temperature. It is a common cooking ingredient in the tropical belt of Africa, Southeast Asia and parts of Brazil, an important foaming agent in soap and detergents, transesterifies to methyl ester, and forms the base for biodiesel. The palm oil industry is a significant contributor to deforestation in the tropics where palms are grown and has been cited as a factor in social problems due to allegations of human rights violations among growers.
*this is updated in another file*

The Refinery is an optional and sometimes unneccesary Building, but the Palm Mill is quite the opposite. Although limited in number, you will want every last copy of this Unique Component. Perhaps the most signficant bonus is the extra Oil copies, which can even help secure the next tier of Monopoly bonus, so you will want the Building in a City with a large Population. There are also significant yield bonuses on offer for Plantations and Lumbermills (though note the reduction in Food, which goes against the first bonus somewhat) which might influence your choice of location, as well as boosts to Sea Trade Routes. Whatever your preferred use case, you will need Jungle to make it a reality, so if you have not got enough, you'll have to go looking for it!
Karaoke Lounge

Karaoke is a type of interactive entertainment system usually offered in nightclubs and bars, where people sing along to pre-recorded accompaniment using a microphone. Its musical content is an instrumental rendition of a well-known popular song. In recent times, lyrics are typically displayed on a video screen, along with a moving symbol, changing colour, or music video images, to guide the singer. The global karaoke market has been estimated to be worth nearly $10 billion. The precursors of karaoke machines using cassette tapes made their first appearances in Japan and the Philippines in the 1970s. Commercial versions manufactured by Japanese companies using LaserDisc became available worldwide in the 1980s, leading to a surge in popularity.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In Asia, a karaoke box is the most popular type of karaoke venue. A karaoke box is a small or medium-sized room containing karaoke equipment rented by the hour or half-hour, providing a more intimate atmosphere. Karaoke venues of this type are often dedicated businesses, some with multiple floors and a variety of amenities including food service, but hotels and business facilities sometimes provide karaoke boxes as well. In South Korea, karaoke boxes are called noraebangs. In mainland China and Taiwan, a karaoke establishment is called a KTV.
*this is updated in another file*

The Karaoke Lounge is the final weapon in the war for the Cultural Victory. The first bonus is a boost to Musicians, which generates the Great Person that has the most direct effect on Tourism output. The second are bonuses to wide Empires, with instant Tourism and yields to Musicians' Guilds scaling with the size of your Empire. The third is the other side of that coin, with big boosts when Citizens are born in your Cities, allowing you to direct Food to your high-Tourism City or Cities in order to eke out every last drop of offensive advantage.
Sun Dance Site

The Sun Dance is a North American ceremony practiced primarily by the Plains cultures, as well as a new movement within Native American religions. Members of otherwise independent bands gather to reaffirm beliefs about the world and the supernatural through rituals of personal and community sacrifice. Typically, young men would dance semi-continuously for several days and nights without eating or drinking; in some cultures self-mortification is/was also practiced. Ceremonial pipes are also commonly employed, with the smoke believed to carry prayers to the attention of the Creator or other powerful animal spirits.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Typically, the Sun Dance is a grueling ordeal for the dancers, a physical and spiritual test that they offer in sacrifice for their people. Young men dance around a pole to which they are fastened by "rawhide thongs pegged through the skin of their chests" until they collapse and their skin was torn loose. Family members and friends stay in the surrounding camp and pray in support of the dancers. Communities plan and organize for at least a year to prepare for the ceremony.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Sun Dances were often used in relation to military endeavors, serving to grant spiritual power, reinforcing community strength in a time of conflict, but also to obtain knowledge of the future. Before the Battle of Little Bighorn, Sitting Bull had a Sun Dance vision where mounted U.S. soldiers fell upside down from the sky into their camp. He interpreted this as a message from Wakan Tanka, or the Great Spirit Creator, that American soldiers would attack them but be annihilated by the warriors in a victorious battle.
*this is updated in another file*

In the City your designate to have the Sun Dance Site, "We Love the King Day" is more effective and you can manually activate it by performing a Public Works for when you cannot get hold of the required Resource. You will also single that City out to grant a powerful set of Promotions for your Melee, Gun, and Recon Units. The most obvious candidate for this National Wonder is therefore the Capital, but you have to bear in mind the additional demands on Production you are placing that you might otherwise want to spread out amongst other Cities whilst focussing on other infrastructure and Wonders.
Floating Market

A floating market is a market where goods are sold from boats. Originating in times and places where water transport played an important role in daily life, they are chiefly found in Myanmar, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, and India. Archaeologists have found evidence that extensive trading networks likely existed in Vietnam's river deltas from as far back as 4,500 years ago. Typical goods on offer include produce, especially fruit like mango and banana, cooked dishes (mostly vegetarian) including desserts like coconut rice dumplings, clothes and hats, candles, handicrafts and paintings. Today, many floating markets operate mainly as tourist attractions.
*this is updated in another file*

The Floating Market gives strong bonuses, but they are limited to particular Terrain and Bonus Resources. A Mandala Civilization should therefore be quick to settle those areas abundant in the Fresh Water they will need to maximize their early-game Unique Component.
Milpa

In agriculture, a milpa is a field for growing food crops and a crop-growing system used throughout Mesoamerica, especially in the Yucatán Peninsula, in Mexico. Based on the agronomy of the Maya and of other Mesoamerican peoples, the milpa system is used to produce crops of maize, beans, and squash without employing artificial pesticides and artificial fertilizers. This is possible using land-conservation and crop rotation. Further, Milpa crops are nutritionally (as well as environmentally) complementary. What is more, Milpa planting involves complex interactions and relationships between farmers that serve to an institution whose religious and social importance often appear to exceed its nutritional and economic importance.
*this is updated in another file*

Since they do not require Horses, Milpa can be built everywhere. Therefore a Mesoamerican player should prepare to have a higher population entering the end game than other Culture Groups, so long as you can obtain enough Cities. To that end, the Milpa becomes stronger the more of them you have, further incentivizing a wide Empire. On top of this, the bonuses of the Agribusiness are extended to Culture and Faith, making Farms more lucrative (relative to, say, Lumbermills) than otherwise.
Archaeological Park

An archaeological park is a site where evidence of past human activity is preserved and open to the public for exploration and education. These parks often feature well-preserved remains, such as buildings, structures, or landscapes, that offer insights into the history and culture of a particular time period. They can be used as tangible examples of cultural tourism, attracting visitors and contributing to the region's economy. As they are often critical to what are often otherwise fragile economies, most modern Levantine states place cultural sites under their own Ministry of Antiquities.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Egypt is the most famous location for archaeological parks, including the Pyramids of Giza and the Sphinx, the Necropolis of Saqqara, the temple complexes at Luxor and Karnak, and the Valley of the Kings all being hugely significant. Less well-travelled are sites in Syria and Iraq, such as Ashur, Erbil Citadel, Hatra, Samarra, Babylon, Nineveh, Ur, and Karbala.
*this is updated in another file*

Archaeology is a small but important system whose unlock signals the final phase of the game. As Archaeology is effectively a race, being able to Dig faster gives you a large advantage both offensively and defensively. Once you have some Artifacts, Archaeological Parks boost their Theming, with twice the bonus if the Artifacts are from your Civilization. If Landmarks are more your speed, especially if you can't get hold of Artifacts from your own Empire, then don't worry because those are boosted too!
Petrochemical Plant

The Middle East is a major hub for both oil production and petrochemical plants, with many OPEC members located in the region. OPEC plays a significant role in regulating oil production and prices, impacting the global oil market and, by extension, the petrochemical industry. The region's focus on downstream refining and petrochemicals is growing, with significant investments and capacity additions planned. It is estimated that 79.5 percent of the world's proven oil reserves are located within OPEC nations, with the Middle East alone accounting for 67.2 percent of OPEC's total reserves.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]In a series of steps in the 1960s and 1970s, OPEC restructured the global system of oil production in favor of oil-producing states and away from an oligopoly of dominant Anglo-American oil firms (the "Seven Sisters"). In the 1970s, restrictions in oil production led to a dramatic rise in oil prices with long-lasting and far-reaching consequences for the global economy. Since the 1980s, OPEC has had a limited impact on world oil-supply and oil-price stability, as there is frequent cheating by members on their commitments to one another, and as member commitments reflect what they would do even in the absence of OPEC.
*this is updated in another file*

Oil is a key part of the end game. A Mid Eastern player will always have access to excess Oil above the usual offering of the Refinery, and that can either be used for diplomatic (and economic) goals or military ones. The Petrochemical Plant also provides Gold and Science, partly from Trade Routes and partly from Oil Improvements themselves. Acquiring more Oil is usually running contrary to enjoying many active International Trade Routes, so exploiting both benefits will require careful strategy.
Metalsmith

Bronze technology came to Britain long before the second millennium BC, but it was not until the coming of the British Iron Age, around 500 BC, that the insular tradition of bronzesmithing (as well as goldsmithing) achieved true preeminence. British metalwork, and that of Continental Gaul, developed along roughly parallel lines until the second century BC. In its infancy Celtic an borrowed heavily from Greek and Estruscan designs but evolved a uniquely Celtic sensibility known today as La Tene.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The Early Medieval art of Britain and Ireland, which produced the Book of Kells and other masterpieces, and is what "Celtic art" evokes for much of the general public in the English-speaking world, is called Insular art in art history. Archaeologists generally use "Celtic" to refer to the culture of the European Iron Age from around 1000 BC onwards, until the conquest by the Roman Empire. The Celtic Revival from the 18th century to the modern era, which began as a conscious effort by Modern Celts, mostly in the British Isles, to express self-identification and nationalism is still popular today, from Celtic cross funerary monuments to interlace tattoos.
*this is updated in another file*

The key output of the Metalsmith -- additional Culture -- comes from working Mines, so before the Medieval the Celtic player should look to settling Cities with a good number of Hill tiles. For every City you will receive a random Metal; with few Cities this is of marginal benefit but when you cross a critical threshold you can gain control of Global Monopolies, giving a unique path toward economic dominance.
Mead Hall

A mead hall or feasting hall was a large building with a single room intended to receive guests and serve as a center of community social life. From the fifth century to the Early Middle Ages such a building was the residence of a lord or king and his retainers. Beer and mead were served on festive occasions, where music was played, poetry was recited, board and dice games were played, and stories were told.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]According to a legend recorded by Snorri Sturluson, in the Heimskringla, the late 9th century Värmlandish chieftain Áki invited both the Norwegian king Harald Fairhair and the Swedish king Eric Eymundsson, but had the Norwegian king stay in the newly constructed and sumptuous one, because he was the youngest one of the kings and the one who had the greatest prospects. The older Swedish king, on the other hand, had to stay in the old feasting hall. The Swedish king was so humiliated that he killed Áki.
*this is updated in another file*

The Mead Hall converts combat XP to Golden Age Points, so the player should look to bonuses that interact with Golden Ages: from early Bath buildings and Beliefs, through to the Artistry and Rationalism trees and beyond. The Mead Hall itself benefits, stacking an increasing bonus that you might even be able to turn into a stepping stone to a Cultural Victory!
Faikava

Kava is used for medicinal, religious, political, cultural, and social purposes throughout the Pacific. The traditional kava beverage is prepared through aqueous extraction of the fresh or dried roots of the Piper methysticum plant. These cultures have a great respect for the plant and place a high importance on it. In Fiji, for example, a formal yaqona (kava) ceremony will often accompany important social, political, or religious functions, usually involving a ritual presentation of the bundled roots as a sevusevu (gift) and drinking of the yaqona itself.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Samoan kawa is served in a polished coconut half called an ipu tau 'ava. The overall ceremony is highly ritualized, with specific gestures and phrases to be used at various times. It is usually mixed by a high chief's daughter at any ceremony. In Tonga, kava may be drunk nightly at kalapu (Tongan for "club"), which is also called a faikava ("to do kava"). In contemporary culture only men drink the kava, although women who serve it may be present. Men talk about politics, sports, tradition & culture, jokes, and will sing traditional love songs, often accompanied by guitar. Some now-famous string bands have had their origin at a faikava.
*this is updated in another file*

With bonuses to "We Love the King Day", you will want to acquire as many Resources as possible, in spite of the potential scarcity in your own islands Empire. Additionally, you can an additional Musician slot in every City, making the Cultural Victory that much more appealing. What is more, Faikava suppresses an Urbanization point, making working that Musician even easier!
Potlatch House

A potlatch is a gift-giving feast practiced by Indigenous peoples of the Pacific Northwest Coast of Canada and the United States, among whom it is traditionally the primary governmental institution, legislative body, and economic system. A potlatch involves giving away or destroying wealth or valuable items in order to demonstrate a leader's wealth and power. Potlatches are also focused on the reaffirmation of family, clan, and international connections, and the human connection with the supernatural world. Potlatch also serves as a strict resource management regime, where coastal peoples discuss, negotiate, and affirm rights to and uses of specific territories and resources. Potlatches often involve music, dancing, singing, storytelling, making speeches, and often joking and games. The honouring of the supernatural and the recitation of oral histories are a central part of many potlatches.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The event was hosted by a numaym, or 'House', a complex cognatic kin group usually headed by aristocrats, but including commoners and occasional slaves. Gifts included storable food (oolichan, or candlefish, oil or dried food), canoes, slaves, and ornamental "coppers". The potlatch was the occasion on which titles associated with masks and other objects were "fastened on" to a new office holder. Two kinds of titles were transferred on these occasions. Firstly, each numaym had a number of named positions of ranked "seats" (which gave them a seat at potlatches) transferred within itself. These ranked titles granted rights to hunting, fishing and berrying territories.
Requires the [COLOR_CULTURE_STORED]Pacific[ENDCOLOR] Cultural Group.

The Potlatch House is unusual, turning the one-off Culture boost of the Circus into a recurring Event that scales with Era. Every time it happens you gain rare yields, including lucrative Great Diplomat Points, but you also lose Gold as your valuables are destroyed! You can claw some of this back from Fish and Deer, which generate additional yields. So consider settling Coasts and Forests to get the most out of your Unique Component.
Reindeer Herding District

Requires the [ICON_CULTURE_JFD_POLAR] [COLOR:182:17:254:255]{TXT_KEY_CULTURE_JFD_POLAR_SHORT_DESC}[ENDCOLOR] Cultural Group.[NEWLINE]Place up to 2 copies of [ICON_RES_REINDEER] Reindeer near the City.

The Agribusiness is a powerful building in Food rich Cities working many Farms and Pastures, but as a Polar Civilization you are unlike to count many such location within your core Empire. Not to worry, the Reindeer Herding District brings additional Resources and Terrains into the list of benefits, actually becoming more powerful the more arctic terrain you have acquired! What is more, they spawn additional bonus Reindeer nearby to improve otherwise barren tiles further. Since the Reindeer Herding District does not require Horses, you should build it everywhere, even though its unique bonuses are restricted to certain biomes.

Reindeer herding is conducted by individuals within some kind of cooperation, in forms such as families, districts, Sámi and Yakut villages and sovkhozy (collective farms). Modern archaeological data (rock art) suggest that domestication may have taken place for the first time in the Sayan Mountains between Russia and Mongolia, possibly 2-3 thousand years ago. Indeed reindeer are the only semi-domesticated animal which naturally belong to the North. Approximately 100,000 people are engaged in reindeer herding today around the circumpolar North, covering vast areas. For example in Sweden, around 55% of the land use is districted for herding Reindeer.
Campsor

Campsores were money changers appearing around 1150 AD who, at the request of merchants, exchanged coins according to the local minting. The ability of the money changers to keep in mind the multiple differences between the coins circulating in the various states was considered a real art, and trod a fine line to not be considered usury. They also offered deposit custody services and paid an interest from ventures, and were therefore the first sort of modern banking entity. This eventually expanded in the Republic of Venice in the 13th Century when its Grain Office did a banking business that included both deposits and lending.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]As Banking in the Renaissance expanded the small-scale money changers either became more free-wheeling pawn-broker adjacent "banchi a minuto" or the more respectable "banchi aperti". The latter's business was done out in the open of a public square, recording all their transactions in a single journal visible on their table or "bancus" which they were required by law to only transfer between accounts when the customers were observing. Similarly, transfers between banchi aperti were done outside, and verbally. Over time, as their influence became international, the incorporated "banchi grossi", like the Banco dei Medici, came to dominate the European economy and the advent of double-entry accounting.
*this is updated in another file*

Campsores add Naval synergies to the Bank, benefitting your Coastal Cities both with yields on infrastructure as well as Production towards ships of all kinds. As such, you will want to value the Coast a lot more. On top of this, Merchants generate some Culture, making them preferred over other Specialists. All these things will get you more Gold but if you need to perform some serious maneuvers your Wealth process will be even more effective.
Festival Plaza

From Mongolia to Anatolia, nomadic peoples enjoy a set of distinctive sports that have their roots in the skills required to survive on the steppe and in the unrivalled equestrian abilities that fuelled successive empires, from the Huns to the Mongols. Large festivals include competitions of several different sports depending on the country, and today there is even an Olympic-like international event called the Nomad Games. There are traditional events such as archery and long-distance horse races, but the games also promote ethnic food, traditional dress, and even the art of epic storytelling.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Axel Heikel of the Finnish expedition to Mongolia wrote about a wrestling competition the expedition witnessed during their ten-day stay in Urga (now Ulaanbaatar, capital of Mongolia) from 27 July until 7 August 1891. The Urga games took place at the old central square which would have been located just to the north of present-day Sükhbaatar Square. Touching the ground with anything other than foot or palm of hand loses the match. Today, amongst other events, the national Naadam tournament still takes place every July.
*this is updated in another file*

The Festival Plaza brings a dual-purpose to the Hotel, in addition to general boosts to Culture and Growth, as well as Happiness to support the new Citizens. Indeed when you grow, even more Production is provided as an instant yield. If you choose to train Units, they will enjoy additional HP, and each one provides a boost of Tourism, feeding back in to the primary role of the Hotel. Note that the percentage boosts to Culture and Growth, as well as the additional Happiness, are contingent on having first an Arena, and then a Stadium. As such the bonus is effectively doubled once you reach Atomic Theory.
East India Company

The Portuguese under Vasco da Gama discovered a naval route to the Indian Ocean through the southern tip of Africa in 1497–98. Although an alliance between the Venetians and Egyptians tried to stop them, during the 16th century the Portuguese had gone as far as to establish bases in the Persian Gulf. After Magellan lost his Portuguese patronage, he became the first European to sail the Pacific Ocean for the Spanish, who first traded with and then seized control of the Philippines and Guam, linking up with Mexico.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]The establishment of the Dutch East India Company in the early 17th century lead to a quick increase in volume of the slave trade in the region; there were perhaps up to 500,000 slaves in various Dutch colonies during the 17th and 18th centuries in the Indian Ocean. In the same period, the (British) East India Company (EIC) was established and in 1622 one of its ships carried slaves from the Coromandel Coast to Dutch East Indies. The EIC mostly traded in African slaves but also some Asian slaves purchased from Indian, Indonesian and Chinese slave traders. The French also established colonies, on the islands of Réunion and Mauritius, in 1721.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]It is hard to express how extraordinarily lucrative trade to the East Indies was in the colonial era. Investors in Francis Drake's 1577-80 voyage received a return of some 5000%. The EIC generated profits from effective monopoly power, particularly in the 18th and 19th centuries, including returns as high as 400% on individual voyages. The Company's business brought in vast quantities of goods like tea, cotton, and spices, and was a major force in the British economy, even funding the Industrial Revolution. The EIC's profits were so significant that it was, at one point, larger than several nations and essentially the de facto emperor of large portions of India.

The first thing to note is that this Unique National Wonder grants yields to Harbors, so think carefully about how to settle as many Coastal Cities as you can get away with. Although the East India Company does not have to be built on Water, and you still receive its global XP bonus wherever you construct it, you can only take advantage of its Sea Route bonuses with a Coastal City. If you picked Tradition, this will almost certainly be the Capital, but if you aren't then pay attention to your distribution of Specialists so as to extract the most value from your Great Person Points.
Baggataway Field

Baggataway is one name for a tribal game played by eastern Woodlands Native Americans and by some Plains Indians tribes in what is now the United States of America and Canada, and is the predecessor of the modern game of Lacrosse. Games were semi-major events that could last several days. As many as 100 to 1,000 men from opposing villages or tribes would participate. The games were played in open plains located between the two villages, and the goals could range from 500 yards (460 m) to 6 miles (9.7 km) apart. There was also a women's version of lacrosse called amtahcha in some areas, which used much shorter sticks with larger heads.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Pregame rituals were very similar to rituals associated with war. Players would decorate their sticks and bodies with paint and charcoal. Before the game, every player was required to place a wager. Items such as handkerchiefs, knives, trinkets and horses were part of the wager. The bets would be displayed on a rack near the spectators, and items would be awarded proportionally to the winner of each quarter.

The Baggataway Field spreads the Culture bonus to Forest and Jungle to Plains tiles (stacking). As Culture on tiles allows you to generate Tourism, this is beneficial in pursuing the Cultural Victory. To aid this, Tourism is also boosted during WLTKD. The building is not completely dedicated to one victory condition, it gives a smaller version of the Stadium Influence boost on completion and, in fact, converts effort spent pursuing City-State alliances into a Unit Production, which can become very large, allowing you to construct and replenish an army either defend your peaceful victory, or to conquer the world!
